predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Attica and Boeotia, conquered by Boniface of Montferrat in November 1204 and granted to Othon de la Roche ('To Othon de la Roche, he gave Athens')

successors.name: Catalan Company
successors.text: Athens and Thebes, surrendered to the Catalan Company after Halmyros (15 March 1311); the Duchy's land from 1311, which Cliopatria's Catalan Company row picks up only in 1314

ledger.x: 1205: Othon de la Roche establishes the Lordship of Athens, with Thebes.

c. 1211: Othon holds Thebes. Emperor Henry took Thebes from Albertino of Canossa on 8 May 1209; 'it is unclear whether Henry then gave Thebes to Othon in 1209 or whether it was not granted until before 1211' and the lead has Othon acquiring it 'by around 1211'. Thebes became 'his capital and economic centre'. The year…
1258: Achaean army crosses the Isthmus into Attica and Boeotia.
1258: Karydi ends the war on the Athenian front.
1260: Guy I is Duke of Athens.
1309: the Brienne succeed the de la Roche.

wars.name: War of the Euboeote Succession
wars.outcome: Achaean victory at Karydi (May/June 1258); Guy I submitted and was pardoned by Louis IX, who made him duke; the 1262 treaty restored the status quo ante bellum.

wars.name: Catalan Company conquest of Athens (Battle of Halmyros)
wars.outcome: Catalan victory at Halmyros on 15 March 1311; Walter V killed; Athens surrendered by his widow; the Catalans took the Duchy except Argos and Nauplia.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary: the Duchy is 'the Attic peninsula as well as Boeotia'.
